title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page classifies when a quadratic extension B = A[S]/(S^2 - a) of a regular local ring A is normal or regular, including residue characteristic 2. That page then parametrizes quadratic covers of P^1_Z by classes in Q(t)^*/Q(t)^{*2}. Each class has a unique representative P = ±qQ, with q a squarefree positive integer and Q a primitive polynomial in Z[t] that is squarefree in Q[t] and has positive leading coefficient.

This page: which of these covers have generically étale fibres over every prime p, and when is the cover étale away from a divisor?

(1) Odd p. The fibre S^2 - P(T) = 0 over F_p[T] is generically étale iff P ≢ 0 mod p. So no odd prime divides q, hence q ∈ {1,2}.

(2) p = 2, case q = 2. Work in the DVR O = Z[T]_(2), with m = (2). Then a = 2Q lies in m \ m^2, so B is normal (even regular) at the generic point of the fibre at 2. But it is totally ramified there, so the fibre is not generically étale. Hence q = 1.

(3) p = 2, case q = 1. The equation S^2 - εQ is purely inseparable mod 2, so B itself never has generically étale fibre at 2. One must pass to the normalization. By the previous page's analysis, the normalization is étale at the generic point of the fibre at 2 iff εQ is the square of a unit modulo m^2 = (4) in O. In that case write εQ = α^2 - b with b ∈ 4O. Then U = (S - α)/2 satisfies U^2 + αU + b/4 = 0, an Artin–Schreier type equation that is separable mod 2.

(4) The sign ε is determined by Q. If both Q and -Q were squares mod 4 in O, then -1 would be a square mod 4. But u^2 ≡ -1 mod 2 forces u = 1 + 2v, and then u^2 ≡ 1 mod 4. Grothendieck asserts the condition is also sufficient.

(5) Example. Take Q = T(T - λ), with λ = 2^α 3^β; the intended case is λ = 1728 = 2^6·3^3, the exceptional j-invariant. If 4 | λ then Q ≡ T^2 mod 4, so ε = +1. Conversely, if λ is odd, Q mod 2 is not a square. If λ ≡ 2 mod 4, then R ≡ T mod 2 gives R^2 ≡ T^2 mod 4 ≢ T^2 - 2T. So 4 | λ is necessary and sufficient.

Passing to T' = 1/T gives T(T - λ) = T^2(1 - λT'). The double cover becomes S'^2 = 1 - λT' over Spec Z[T']_{λT' - 1} = P^1_Z \ {0, λ}, in the original coordinate T. Its normalization is given by U^2 + U + (λ/4)T' = 0, with discriminant 1 - λT'. This is a finite étale double cover of P^1_Z minus the two sections T = 0 and T = λ, which meet over the primes dividing λ (here 2 and 3).

Purpose. This explores étale covers of the arithmetic j-line over Z minus {0, 1728}, for the project on moduli of elliptic curves.
errors: Sign slip: with ε = +1 one gets T(T - λ) = T^2(1 - λT'), so the equation should be S^2 = 1 - λT', not S^2 = λT' - 1. The latter is -1 times a square mod 4 and is not étale at 2.

Garbled sentence 'il faut que B(p) soit normal que P soit un carré mod 4'. The precise condition is that the normalization of B be generically étale over the fibre at 2. B itself is not normal there in this case.
'Carré mod 4' must be understood in the DVR Z[T]_(2), i.e. modulo m^2 = (4), as the square of a unit. Grothendieck does not spell this out.

Sufficiency of the condition ('aussi suffisante') is asserted without proof. It is easy: the Artin–Schreier normalization is separable at the generic point of the fibre at 2, and odd fibres are handled by q = 1.

ideas.what: Classification of quadratic covers of P^1_Z with generically étale fibres at all primes: P = εQ with q = 1, and εQ a unit square mod 4 at the 2-adic generic point
ideas.modern_name: ramification of quadratic extensions in residue characteristic 2; discriminant of the normalization (1+√d)/2-type orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Dedekind/Hilbert theory of quadratic fields, d ≡ 1 mod 4), here transplanted to the function field Q(t)

ideas.what: Explicit finite étale double cover U^2 + U + (λ/4)T' = 0 of P^1_Z minus two sections that meet over the primes dividing λ (λ = 1728)
ideas.modern_name: Artin–Schreier/Kummer double cover over Z; étale covers of arithmetic surfaces / P^1_Z minus sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (the 4 | λ analogue of the 1 - 4x discriminant)

ideas.what: Application to the j-line over Z minus {0, 1728} in the moduli study of elliptic curves over Z
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic of the coarse moduli space of M_{1,1} over Z; étale covers of the j-line over Spec Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur (moduli over Z); specific example unsure

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard computations about quadratic ramification at 2, applied to an explicit étale double cover of P^1_Z minus {0, 1728}. The page offers a glimpse of Grothendieck around 1981 thinking about étale covers of the arithmetic j-line over Z, but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read 'Cette extension est génér^t étale ssi P(T) ≢ 0 (p)'.
'Exemple (... modulaires des courbes elliptiques)' plausibly reads '(Exemple: invariants modulaires des courbes elliptiques)'; the crossed-out word is uncertain.
'λ = 2^α 3^β' is correct: the exceptional modular invariant 1728 = 2^6 3^3.
The last line is 'en normalisant Z[T']_(λT'-1) dans Z[T']_(λT'-1)[S]/(S^2 - (λT'-1))'. The mathematically correct radicand is 1 - λT'.
'E^1_Z' denotes the affine line (𝔼^1_Z) in Grothendieck's notation.
